the runt bastard no one wanted

installer · M-VAVE FM-1

v0.4.5 · 2026-11-21

Installs the DØG-5 firmware on an M-VAVE FM-1 over USB-MIDI. One page, no server: the package is inside this file. Chrome or Edge only.

Tested on one unit, with the older flash chip. DØG-5 was built and tested on a real FM-1 whose flash chip is the Puya P25Q80 (JEDEC 0x856014): installed with this page from the stock firmware, over another firmware from the Firmware Hub and back again, and played across several test builds (12–21 Nov 2026). Newer FM-1s carry a UC25HQ80 chip (JEDEC 0xB36014). The update loader accepts it, but nobody has installed or played DØG-5 on one yet, so how it behaves there (saving, updates, everything) is unknown. If you have a newer unit, keep M-Flasher and your backup ready, and please report what happens.

What can be written (the target range)

Flash rangeWhat happens
0x000000–0x003FFFBoot head (bootloader, chip key). Never written by the update loader.
0x004000–0x092FFFThe app area. The update loader rewrites only the 4 KB sectors that differ, and reads each one back.
0x0E0000–0x0E4FFFStep 1 only: a staged copy of the loader and its update record, written by the firmware that is running now, erased when the update finishes.
everything elseNot written.

This page cannot write flash. It answers the unit's read requests with bytes from the package, and refuses a request outside the package. The loader checks the package against this unit's own chip key before it erases anything (source: firmware/loader/ldr_core.c). Step 1 is done by the unit's running firmware; for a stock unit that code is not in this repository, so what it does is unverified here.

Before you start

The unit

Not looked for yet. Finding it asks the browser for MIDI + SysEx permission, and sends one identity question (a handshake) to the chosen port. Nothing is written.

Install

Last check before the first byte.
Idle.
Bring this tab back to the front. The install keeps running, but in a background tab Chrome can slow it down until the unit gives up. If the unit shows UPDATE FAILED, leave it plugged in, press Find my FM-1 and then Resume.

Dry run

If something goes wrong

Unplug the USB cable, power-cycle the FM-1, and run this page again. A unit that was cut off in step 2 starts in update mode; this page then offers Resume. If the unit will not boot, use M-Flasher with your backup. Nothing more ambitious than that is promised here: app-level USB rescue is unproven on this hardware.

Used on a real FM-1 (older flash chip, see the top of the page) from Chrome on macOS. It runs from https:// or http://localhost (WebMIDI's rule); a downloaded copy of this file works the same when served that way, and makes no network request of any kind.
